newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania company completes tax-exempt issues.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania company completes tax-exempt issues.

text.p: Adult Communities Total Services Inc, a not-for-profit Pennsylvania company that runs continuing care retirement communities, said it has refinanced $142.24 million of outstanding debt with tax-exempt bonds issued in Florida, North Carolina and Pennsylvania.
In a telephone interview Thursday, company finance Vice President Jerry Grant said the transaction is believed to be the largest of its type in the senior living industry.

The four-part deal included $71.12 million of tax-exempt bonds issued by the Montgomery County, Pa., Industrial Development Authority; $37.655 million of variable rate tax-exempt bonds issued by the North Carolina Medical Care Commission and Local Government Commission; $24.215 million of tax-exempt bonds issued by the Palm Beach County, Fla., Health Facilities Authority; and $9.25 of corporate general obligation bonds.
None of the three municipal issuers have any debt service responsibility.
"They were simply acting as a conduit," Grant said.
The Internal Revenue Service allowed the company to enter the tax-exempt arena because of its status as a not-for-profit organization, Grant said.

The company operates 15 facilities in the three states. The transaction converted the company's taxable debt, including mortgages, construction loans with commercial banks and insurance companies and a senior note that was placed privately with the Pennsylvania school teachers retirement fund.

Only one portion of the outstanding debt, a $26.955 million issue for the Brittany Point Estates facility in Pennsylvania, was previously tax-exempt. That issue was advance refunded, lowering interest costs from over 8 percent to about 6 percent, Grant said.

The transaction was complicated because of the number of issuers involved. In Pennsylvania and North Carolina, the debt involved projects within the municipal issuers' boundaries. The Florida issue refinanced debt on a facility in Indian River County, which has an interlocal agreement with the issuer in Palm Beach County.

Overall, the conversion to tax-exempt debt reduced the company's borrowing costs from about 10.5 percent to just under 6 percent, the company said. Adult Communities Total Services is headquartered in West Point, Pa.
